headline: Penguins’ Malkin, Korczak out day-to-day with lower-body injuries
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Penguins forwards Evgeni Malkin and Korczak are out day-to-day with lower-body injuries, and that Elmer Soderblom's status has been changed to week-to-week.

Soderblom's quiet start hides decent underlying play. He has no goals and one assist in six games so far this season, but his own expected goals (the quality of his chances) are 1.45, so he is 1.45 goals short of what those chances usually produce. At 5-on-5, PIT has taken 76 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is about 25 points better with him than without. His absence costs depth more than scoring, and it comes while PIT (5-7-2) sits near even at 49 percent of expected goals. Going by games already played without him, Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Dewar and Lizotte, Malkin is up to 17:08 a night from 14:56, and Tommy Novak is up to 17:31 from 15:25. That plan now has Malkin's own injury hanging over it.
